front: What are the two architectural approaches to multimodal retrieval covered on this page?
back: A unified embedding space (one CLIP-family model puts text and images in the same vector space) versus separate per-modality indexes combined by fusion (e.g. RRF).

front: Which embedding model won the 3-way test, and by how much on text Recall@3?
back: jina-clip-v2 -- it doubled base CLIP's text Recall@3 (0.375 to 0.75) at the same image-matching accuracy (2 of 4).

front: How did SigLIP perform compared to base CLIP, despite being the newer, more-cited model?
back: Worse on both axes: 0.25 text Recall@3 (vs. CLIP's 0.375) and only 1 of 4 correct image matches (vs. CLIP's 2 of 4) -- newer/more-cited isn't automatically better, only measuring settles it.

front: What is the measured cost of the unified approach, even using the best model tested?
back: 25 points of Recall@3 lost on plain factual text questions (1.000 to 0.750) with jina-clip-v2 -- any text encoder good enough to share a space with images trades away text-specific retrieval quality to do it.

front: Why can RRF fusion never let an image outright outrank text at rank 1?
back: 1/(k+0+1) is mathematically identical regardless of which modality occupies rank 1 of its own list -- a structural tie, since RRF is a rank-based consensus mechanism, not a magnitude comparator.

front: What causes RRF to sometimes surface an irrelevant image in the fused top-3?
back: With a small image pool, the least-irrelevant image still becomes 'rank 1' in its list and earns a real fusion score even though its similarity is genuine noise -- a minimum similarity threshold gating fusion fixes this.

Text and image embeddings occupy structurally separate regions of the shared vector space, an artifact of how contrastive vision-language models are trained -- a better model narrows it but doesn't close it.

front: What's the recommended default approach, and when should the unified approach be used instead?
back: Separate indexes + RRF fusion is the default (full text quality, correct text-only routing); use a unified space only when an image must be able to outrank text outright in one open ranking.
